data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004's evidence criterion is non-discriminating for the population of real checklists. A well-designed explicit checklist for tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes is typically *intentionally consistent* (it is engineered to be), so by SRC_004's own countercondition the test has no errors to detect and yields no evidence in the common case. More importantly, a merely-compliant panel and a reliable panel produce the *same observable behavior* on a consistent checklist (both execute the items and reach the verifiable outcome); the distinguishing evidence SRC_004 needs (flagging a runtime error) is absent because there is no error to flag. Thus for the large class of consistent checklists, SRC_004 provides no way to distinguish compliance from reliability, leaving the problem's central question unanswered for those tasks.
